text:
Ben Kindel is a 19-year-old rookie playing 17 and a half minutes a night on a Penguins team that keeps losing, and his numbers carry the weight of both facts. Eight points in 16 games looks modest. The more telling figure is this one: the Penguins have scored 10.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, the biggest gap our numbers flag for him and the kind that usually swings back.

His own finishing is about where it should be (4 goals on 4.5 expected goals), so this is not a shooter running cold. It's a line that creates enough and keeps watching the puck stay out. He scored on the power play in Wednesday's shootout win in San Jose, his first goal since late October.

The 11th pick in 2025 put up 99 points in his last WHL season, and forwards picked in his range usually start around 0.37 points a game. He's at 0.50. When the bounces even out, that number climbs.
headline: Kindel has been better than his line
